what: M5 box 4's running half, and box 5 on a real device: the client's debug APK, built from `testing`, installed and driven on an Android emulator against a real Adjutant server.

host.emulator: user systemd unit `phonon-emulator`, AVD `phonon_test` (Android API 35, google_apis, x86_64), headless (`-no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect`)

artifact.note: the branch head that merged `testing` into the MCP branch; `git diff --stat 406c315 d613a34` is EMPTY, so this APK's source tree is identical to `testing` at d613a34
artifact.build: git clone https://github.com/chezgoulet/adjutant && git checkout 406c315 && cd client && flutter pub get && flutter build apk --debug

server.where: mikoa, LAN 192.168.1.7:8787 — the same ./target/debug/adjutant CI's live harness builds (no Rust differs between 2e5663e and d613a34)
server.database: adjutant_client_live on the local PostgreSQL 18 (the client live harness's own database, bootstrap chief `client-harness-chief`)
server.env: ADJUTANT_DEV_HEADERS=false (the spoofable dev-header stub is off, so the session the app holds is one the server issued), ADJUTANT_RATE_MAX=0 (the run issues a burst), ADJUTANT_ALLOW_SUPERUSER=true (this throwaway test database's role is a superuser)
server.address_typed_in_the_app: http://192.168.1.7:8787 (debug build, so cleartext is allowed — release builds require https by design)

observations.saw: Server / Username / Password on the login form; the app then reached the server and signed in as `client-harness-chief` (the first-run plugin wizard appeared next, and the dashboard after it)

server data rendered on the device: Active missions 0, Members 1, Upcoming events 0, Open motions 1; 'No missions yet'; snackbar 'This deployment now runs 2 plugin(s).' — see finding F1 for that number
observations.nav: 8 destinations: Dashboard, Inbox, Missions, Calendar, Shop, Equipment, Members, Settings

observations.saw: the roster row the server stored: 'Harness Scout' / 'Beacon' / 'Harness Patrol · Harness Lodge' / Active
amber banner 'Offline — showing data from 08:06' and the same roster row from the cache — the read cache on a real device, not a mock

observations.screen: Inbox, with the server STOPPED, after tapping 'Mark read' on a published notice
observations.saw: snackbar 'Offline — your receipt is queued and will sync.'; the shell's app bar carries the pending-write badge (1) beside the offline icon; the notice is STILL shown unread ('1 unread of 1 in this inbox', 'Mark read') — the client did not apply the write locally

observations.screen: Inbox, with the server back, after tapping the app bar's retry
observations.saw: snackbar '1 sent.' and the offline icon gone — the queue replayed the recorded request
'0 unread of 1 in this inbox', the card now offering 'Mark unread', and the inbox badge gone — the device agrees with the server again

server_side_proof.note: `read_via: flutter` is the body the queued entry recorded ({'via': 'flutter'}), so the receipt the server holds is the one the device queued while offline — not a second one written after reconnecting.

findings.F1: The first-run plugin wizard's 'Skip for now' RECORDS a choice: `GET /api/plugins/choice` then read {"plugin_ids":["auth","membership"],"source":"wizard"}, and the twelve other plugins' routes stopped answering at runtime (GET /api/announcements/announcements -> 404 {"error":"route not found"}) while `GET /api/plugins` still listed all fourteen as loaded. On a real deployment this is a footgun: a skip is not a skip, and the plugin list contradicts what is running. Restoring the choice (PUT /api/plugins/choice with all fourteen) brought every route back, 200.
findings.F2: A 404 from the API is rendered by the client as an offline condition: the announcements screen showed 'Cannot reach the server — route not found' for an ApiException(404). A route that is gone is not a network that is down, and the Retry button cannot fix it.
findings.F3: After the shell's queue retry reported '1 sent.', no screen was told to re-read: the Inbox still said '1 unread of 1' (and the nav badge still showed 1) until the destination was re-entered, at which point the truth appeared. Nothing is lost — the counts are the server's and the next read is right — but the interval is user-visible.
findings.F4: The emulator's clock is UTC-4 against the server's UTC, so the cache banner's '08:06' is 12:06 server time: the banner is honest about when the data was written, in the device's own local time.

not_proven: A physical device. This is an x86_64 emulator with a debug build; no phone held it.
A release-signed APK. The release build refuses cleartext http by design (client/lib/api/server_address.dart), so a release APK needs the https deployment to be useful.
That CI performs any of this. The `client` job builds web + a debug APK (#119) and never installs one on a device — the self-hosted runner on this host has no Android job in this repository today.
The APK being attached to a release. The release workflow still attaches only the web bundle.
